evidence: Clear separation of concerns into logical modules: models/, strategies/, api_server.py, auto_trader.py, database.py, etc.
Single executable entry point (crypto_trading.py / __main__.py) with no inter-process communication patterns
Shared in-memory data structures (SQLAlchemy ORM models) across modules, indicating tight coupling within process
No evidence of network-based service boundaries or distributed deployment (e.g., no gRPC, REST clients between core modules)
Database and API clients (BinanceAPIManager, Database) are tightly integrated with business logic (AutoTrader, strategies)
Strategies inherit from AutoTrader, indicating shared core behavior and tight coupling between layers
Single codebase with internal imports (relative imports within binance_trade_bot package) and no service discovery or external service contracts
risks: Tight coupling between strategies and core trading logic may reduce testability and flexibility
Monolithic deployment may limit scalability and independent evolution of components
Shared database session across modules increases risk of transactional anomalies and concurrency issues
